top.title: Osun LG Crisis Will Be Fully Resolved In The Next One Week — Gov Adeleke
top.description: Governor Ademola Adeleke has assured the people of Osun State that the protracted local government crisis in the state will be resolved within the next week, following President Bola Tinubu’s intervention. Governor Adeleke gave this assurance in his inaugural speech during his second-term inauguration held at Osogbo City Stadium, where he listed some of the priorities of his second-term administration across all sectors. “I am glad to announce that Mr President has intervened in the local government matter and in the next one week, the crisis will be fully resolved. Once this is done, our administration will ensure the rehabilitation of the remaining 102 primary health care centres,” he said. Osun Governor Ademola Adeleke was sworn in as governor for a second term on November 27, 2026. Photo: Femi Ojomo/Channels Television. As part of his priorities, the re-elected governor promised to set up the Osun State Electricity Regulatory Commission, as well as infrastructural expansion and recruitment of teachers and rehabilitation of schools, including reviving technical colleges. He also said that job and wealth creation will be at the heart of his second term. “We will establish a digital hub in each of our three senatorial districts. This is to drive job creation in the digital economy,” Adeleke said. “In education, we will recruit more teachers and speed up school rehabilitation. We will expand bursaries and scholarships, keep tuition affordable, tackle cultism, and revive our technical colleges.” In the health sector, he said about 70 per cent of existing primary health care centres were rehabilitated and equipped with solar and power facilities in his first term. “We upgraded and completed 232 out of 332 primary health care centres. The plan was to complete the whole 332 PHCs, but the seizure of local government allocations halted the process,” the governor said. “My government made sure that our primary school teachers, healthcare professionals at our primary healthcare centres, and local government retirees got paid in the last two years.” Osun Governor Ademola Adeleke sworn in as governor for a second term on November 27, 2026. Photo: Femi Ojomo/Channels Television. Adeleke said his vision is to move Osun from a civil service economy to an industrialised one, noting that his administration is open to partnership with private organisations and economic advisory groups. “Specifically, we will target agro-processing factories, industrial parks across districts, free trade zones, sports and tourism development, and a better business environment. “Fellow citizens, we must heal the wounds of the past and unite for our collective good. I charge the Osun political class to embrace elite consensus, transparency, good governance and local content,” he added. President Tinubu was represented at the inauguration by the Vice President, Kashim Shettima. Other dignitaries that graced the occasion included Bisi Akande and Iyiola Omisore, other All Progressives

top.title: Russia’s VTB Opens Bitcoin Trading as Central Bank Finalizes Crypto Test
top.description: Bitcoin Magazine Russia’s VTB Opens Bitcoin Trading as Central Bank Finalizes Crypto Test Russian bank VTB began letting brokerage clients buy and sell bitcoin in its investing app on Friday, a day after the Bank of Russia approved the knowledge test every Russian crypto buyer now has to pass. Starting Nov. 27, clients of VTB’s brokerage can trade cryptocurrencies in the VTB My Investments app, the broker said . For now, the trades happen over the counter rather than on an exchange, and access is limited to qualified investors, the legal term for Russians who meet wealth or experience thresholds, who also pass the new test. “In our model, access to cryptocurrencies will require qualified investor status and passing special testing,” Andrei Yatskov, head of brokerage services at VTB, said . He said the test would appear in the app on Nov. 27 and work like the bank’s existing tests for other instruments. VTB handles the buying, storage and record-keeping itself on Russian infrastructure. To trade, clients need to open a separate digital account at VTB’s digital depository, where the crypto is held, on top of their regular brokerage account. The bank received its digital depository and crypto exchange licenses on Oct. 6. “At the start, we will focus on buying and selling cryptocurrencies, and then we will introduce additional services as regulation develops,” Yatskov said. Eight questions before the first trade The launch came quickly after the regulator moved. On Nov. 26, the Bank of Russia approved the first basic standards for brokers and crypto exchange offices, setting the rules for the test. Every investor has to take it, qualified or not, and it is free. Buyers must answer at least seven of eight questions correctly. The standard lays out eight topic blocks, from regulation, technical basics and information security to stablecoins, low-liquidity coins, address labeling and blocked transactions, and volatility, with one question drawn at random from each. Investors who fail can try once more the same day, with different questions. Brokers are barred from sharing the correct answers with clients or telling them which questions they missed. A passing result stays valid for one year from the test date or the latest trade, whichever comes later. The test was the missing piece for Russian banks. When retail buying became legal on Nov. 17 , T-Bank said it was waiting on a market standard for testing, and VTB said it was waiting on the remaining rules. Under the broker standard, the industry’s self-regulatory organization has three working days after publication to send brokers the answer options and correct answers. Ordinary investors still face tight limits once they pass. Non-qualified buyers can only purchase bitcoin, ether and Tether’s USDT, and no more than 300,000 rubles a year through a single intermediary. SPB Exchange sets Dec. 1 start Exchange trading is next. top.title: Real Madrid set to block exit of four players in January; two allowed to leave – report
top.description: Real Madrid set to block exit of four players in January; two allowed to leave – report With the January transfer window just around the corner, Real Madrid are bracing themselves for relative peace and quiet, especially after a busy summer. The club are not expected to sign any new players in the winter transfer window. However, it is worth mentioning that a series of existing stars are facing an uncertain future and could leave in January. Endrick, Thiago Pitarch and Brahim Diaz are some of the many Real Madrid players facing an uncertain future at Santiago Bernabeu. Real Madrid, though, have a plan. Four exits to be blocked According to Miguel Serrano (h/t Defensa Central ), Real Madrid have made their mind up, as far as the club’s dealings in the January transfer window is concerned. The club are expected to block the exit of all the players who have been linked with a move away from Bernabeu this season, including Endrick. Brahim Diaz won’t be allowed to leave Real Madrid in January. (Photo by Fran Santiago/Getty Images) The exits of Trent Alexander-Arnold, Pitarch and Diaz are also expected to be blocked, as Jose Mourinho consider all of them key parts of the setup. It appears Mourinho is wary that any injury crisis during the second half of the campaign could make these players handy, as they offer plenty of quality to the table. Endrick, in particular, boasts immense talent and has been linked with a move away. But he has the backing of Mourinho . The same goes for Pitarch, even though the midfielder has barely played any football this season. Two exceptions to Real Madrid Serrano adds that Real Madrid have made an exception to this policy for two players in the form of Ferland Mendy and Raul Asencio. Both these defenders are allowed to leave the club in the January transfer window, having failed to find themselves in Mourinho’s plans this season. Ferland Mendy is no longer needed at Real Madrid. (Photo by Jose Manuel Alvarez Rey/Getty Images) Asencio, for one, has struggled with injuries and several off-field controversies. He has also looked like a shadow of his former self. His departure, therefore, could be a major positive for Real Madrid. Mendy, on the other hand, has a lucrative salary at Bernabeu despite having his entire career at Real Madrid marred by injuries . With Marc Cucurella and Alvaro Carreras, Real Madrid look quite stacked at left-back and no longer require the services of Mendy, whose contract expires in 2028. These are, however, still early days and if a lucrative market opportunity comes, Real Madrid will not shy away from making a few more exceptions.

top.description: FC Cincinnati stunned Major League Soccer experts with its 1-0 win over Nashville SC in the first game of their best-of-three playoff series at Nashville’s GEODIS park. They will now have two chances to move on to the Eastern Conference semifinals. The first is at home, 6:30 p.m. Nov. 28 at TQL Stadium. Game 3, if needed, will be 8 p.m. Dec. 2 back in Nashville. As the No. 9 seed in the Eastern Conference, this will be the last home game for Cincinnati in the conference playoffs. The only team in the Western Conference they could host in the MLS Cup final is Real Salt Lake, the No. 9 seed. The team is ready for what could be their last home game. “Trying to make sure that we step on the field with a really strong mindset,” said head coach Pat Noonan. “I know there's confidence, but there's also still a respect factor for how strong Nashville is, and we need to find ways to have our fan base lively, and a lot of times that comes with our play. But Cincinnati served notice with its defense the rest of the way, shutting out the best regular-season team in MLS history. Nashville had 22 shots, six on goal. One arrived to dictate terms with timing and angles, and the other came to bulldoze straight through them. It was a masterclass in craft over chaos from start to finish. top.title: Eagles coach Nick Sirianni celebrates wild Thanksgiving win in Cowboys fans’ faces
top.description: Sirianni celebrates Nick Sirianni gave Cowboys fans some salt for their Thanksgiving meals. Sirianni’s celebration was filled with some one-finger salutes from the Cowboys faithful and a short-lived one, as he was whisked away by Philadelphia’s chief security officer “Big Dom” DiSandro before things got too hairy. Nick Sirianni celebrated in front of the Cowboys fans after the Eagles comeback win ( FOX) pic.twitter.com/mR8isTM2Zh — SportsCenter (@SportsCenter) November 27, 2026 Not that DiSandro didn’t get his licks in. The Herculean 34-year-old was caught trolling former Eagles defensive backs coach and current Cowboys defense coordinator Christian Parker, who recently had his play calling duties taken away by Dallas, before the game, teasing him with an Eagles hat. The win completed the largest-ever Thanksgiving Day comeback in NFL history, with the Eagles trailing 31-10 in the third quarter. Quarterback Joe Milton, in just his third start for Philadelphia — and against his old team — threw for 331 yards and three touchdowns, while adding a rushing score. “He played his butt off,” Sirianni said. “He played really good, made some throws that only he can make. He played an outstanding game, was super composed throughout, played the next play consistently.” Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni reacts after beating the Dallas Cowboys. AP Photo/Sam Hodde His heroics set the stage for veteran kicker Jake Elliott, who drilled a 59-yard field goal to give Philadelphia the miraculous win. “It’s awesome,” Elliott said. “Those are ones that I’ll remember for the rest of my life.” The Eagles, now 4-7, seemingly have life with two straight wins following seven consecutive losses. They remain in the NFC East basement, but beating the rival Cowboys (5-7) definitely provided some fire for Sirianni and his crew.

nigeria.title: Osun LG Crisis Will Be Fully Resolved In The Next One Week — Gov Adeleke
nigeria.description: Governor Ademola Adeleke has assured the people of Osun State that the protracted local government crisis in the state will be resolved within the next week, following President Bola Tinubu’s intervention. Governor Adeleke gave this assurance in his inaugural speech during his second-term inauguration held at Osogbo City Stadium, where he listed some of the priorities of his second-term administration across all sectors. “I am glad to announce that Mr President has intervened in the local government matter and in the next one week, the crisis will be fully resolved. Once this is done, our administration will ensure the rehabilitation of the remaining 102 primary health care centres,” he said. Osun Governor Ademola Adeleke was sworn in as governor for a second term on November 27, 2026. Photo: Femi Ojomo/Channels Television. As part of his priorities, the re-elected governor promised to set up the Osun State Electricity Regulatory Commission, as well as infrastructural expansion and recruitment of teachers and rehabilitation of schools, including reviving technical colleges. He also said that job and wealth creation will be at the heart of his second term. “We will establish a digital hub in each of our three senatorial districts. This is to drive job creation in the digital economy,” Adeleke said. “In education, we will recruit more teachers and speed up school rehabilitation. We will expand bursaries and scholarships, keep tuition affordable, tackle cultism, and revive our technical colleges.” In the health sector, he said about 70 per cent of existing primary health care centres were rehabilitated and equipped with solar and power facilities in his first term. “We upgraded and completed 232 out of 332 primary health care centres. The plan was to complete the whole 332 PHCs, but the seizure of local government allocations halted the process,” the governor said. “My government made sure that our primary school teachers, healthcare professionals at our primary healthcare centres, and local government retirees got paid in the last two years.” Osun Governor Ademola Adeleke sworn in as governor for a second term on November 27, 2026. Photo: Femi Ojomo/Channels Television. Adeleke said his vision is to move Osun from a civil service economy to an industrialised one, noting that his administration is open to partnership with private organisations and economic advisory groups. “Specifically, we will target agro-processing factories, industrial parks across districts, free trade zones, sports and tourism development, and a better business environment. “Fellow citizens, we must heal the wounds of the past and unite for our collective good. I charge the Osun political class to embrace elite consensus, transparency, good governance and local content,” he added. nigeria.title: Arteta urges Arsenal not to underestimate troubled Man City
nigeria.description: Mikel Arteta insisted Friday that Arsenal will not underestimate spluttering Manchester City in Sunday’s crucial clash with their Premier League title rivals. Arteta’s leaders are six points clear of third-placed City heading into the showdown at the Emirates Stadium. City led the table in the opening months of the season before suffering a major dip in recent weeks. Enzo Maresca’s men have only won just in their last seven games in all competitions and are without a victory in their last four league matches. Arteta cannot explain City’s stumble but he has no intention of taking three points for granted against them. “I don’t know, that’s a question for them. All I can say is when I watch them play, a lot of the games they have to win they do more than the opponent, but this is football,” the Arsenal manager told reporters on Friday. “When we play the home games against big teams that becomes crucial in the title challenge, we know how important those games are. But the second part, we’re in November, and we still have long to play. “The challenge is for us, we cannot control what other opponents are going to do.” City boss Maresca has been criticised for his team’s poor form but Arteta is a firm admirer of the Italian, who is in his first season in charge after replacing Pep Guardiola. “I know Enzo personally and he’s a phenomenal guy. He lives and breathes football, is very analytical. He is already on the great managerial career already. Everything is super positive,” Arteta said. – Arsenal ‘hunger’ – Arsenal sit top despite also being below their peak form in recent weeks. They were held to draws in their last two games against Newcastle in the Premier League and Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League. Prior to that, the Gunners eked out three wins by a one-goal margin and suffered an embarrassing League Cup exit at fourth-tier Fleetwood. Arteta believes Arsenal are still rounding into form and he hopes the motivation of a valuable victory against City will spur them on as they chase the high of a second successive title. “Yes, more hunger to do it again. To have those moments again together,” he said. “Everybody puts in unbelievable shifts every week, to analyse the opponent, to breathe the right atmosphere around the boys and to win the game, week in, week out.” City’s dynastic run under Guardiola is an inspiration to Arteta even if they have lost their way lately. “You certainly learn from that. And that inspires you to go to a different level, and that’s the level Manchester City brought to this league, because what they have done is unprecedented,” he said. Arteta revealed David Raya is back in training after missing the Dortmund game with a shoulder injury suffered against Newcastle. Kepa Arrizabalaga deputised against Dortmund but Arteta would not reveal if Raya is ready to return to action this weekend. nigeria.title: It won’t happen again — Fashola on Peter Obi’s 2023 victory in Lagos
nigeria.description: Former Lagos State Governor Babatunde Fashola has said the All Progressives Congress was caught off guard by Peter Obi’s victory in Lagos during the 2023 presidential election, insisting the party would not allow a repeat in future elections. Obi, who contested on the platform of the Labour Party, defeated APC candidate Bola Tinubu in his home state, securing a narrow victory that stunned the ruling party. Speaking in an exclusive interview with ARISE News, Fashola admitted that the outcome was unexpected, attributing the party’s surprise to pre-election surveys that did not indicate Lagos was at risk. “We were blindsided. It won’t happen again,” he said. Asked whether the APC had underestimated its opponents by taking Lagos for granted, the former governor rejected the suggestion, explaining that the party’s projections had not identified the state as a major battleground. “Lagos didn’t look like a battleground at the time, not from the numbers,” Fashola said. He added, “We do very scientific surveys, and Lagos didn’t look like a battleground in that sense. So that’s why I say I was blindsided, on reflection.” Fashola, however, said the party recovered from the setback shortly after the presidential election, arguing that subsequent electoral outcomes showed it remained politically strong in the state. “In spite of that setback at the presidential election, we turned it around very quickly,” he said. He also dismissed suggestions that Obi’s victory marked a lasting decline in the APC’s influence in Lagos, saying the party should focus on its record and policies rather than dwell on the past. The former governor spoke amid questions about voter intimidation, ethnic rhetoric and violence during the 2023 elections in Lagos, insisting that political competition should not involve threats, attacks or hate speech. Fashola said politicians could aggressively promote their parties and challenge opponents without resorting to personal attacks or inflammatory rhetoric. “You are entitled to very vigorously and vociferously campaign for your party, as I am doing now, and showing what our record is, without damaging anybody’s name, anybody’s reputation, and without hate speech,” he said. He described democracy as a “non-contact sport”, arguing that parties should compete through ideas, policies and performance rather than intimidation or violence. Obado was sentenced on Friday by Kenya’s High Court alongside two former aides who were convicted over the killing of the 26-year-old woman, who was seven months pregnant with his child at the time of her death. His former personal assistant, Michael Oyamo, was also handed a 25-year prison sentence, while former county clerk Caspal Ojwang’ Obiero received 18 years. The court found that Obado supplied the motive and financial resources for the murder, while Oyamo coordinated its execution. According to the BBC, the court established that Obado was unhappy about the pregnancy resulting from his relationship with Otieno. She had reportedly contacted Oduor to discuss her relationship with Obado, who was then serving as governor. Oduor escaped from the abductors by jumping out of the moving vehicle, and his account later provided investigators with an important lead. Otieno’s body was subsequently found near Kodera Forest. A post-mortem examination established that she died from strangulation and excessive bleeding caused by multiple stab wounds. The court also confirmed that Obado was the biological father of her unborn child. Obado and the two former aides were convicted of murder on July 23, 2026, after prosecutors presented 42 witnesses and 81 exhibits during the trial. Before the sentencing, Otieno’s mother appealed to the court for leniency, describing Obado’s imprisonment as “another death in the family”. nigeria.title: Canada lists 28 African countries eligible for special study visa
nigeria.description: Canada has listed 28 African countries whose citizens are eligible to apply for a special study permit programme that offers an opportunity to study in the country and potentially obtain permanent residence after graduation. The initiative, known as the Francophone Minority Communities Student Pilot (FMCSP), targets French-speaking international students seeking admission into selected Canadian post-secondary institutions outside Quebec. According to Canada’s immigration department, Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC), the programme is designed to strengthen French-speaking minority communities by attracting international students who can contribute to their growth. The 28 eligible African countries are Benin, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cabo Verde, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Chad, Comoros, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Republic of the Congo, Côte d’Ivoire, Djibouti, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Madagascar, Mali, Mauritania, Mauritius, Morocco, Niger, Rwanda, São Tomé and Príncipe, Senegal, Seychelles, Togo and Tunisia. Egypt is also eligible but is classified separately under the Middle East. To qualify, applicants must be citizens of one of the eligible countries, demonstrate French-language proficiency of at least level 5 on the NCLC scale in speaking, listening, reading and writing, and secure admission into a participating Canadian institution. They must also enrol in a full-time post-secondary programme lasting at least two years, leading to a diploma or degree, with more than 50 per cent of classes taught in French. Applicants must demonstrate sufficient funds to cover tuition, living expenses and transportation. The programme’s 2026–2027 intake opened on August 26, 2026, with a limit of 2,970 study permit applications until August 25, 2027. Among the participating institutions are the University of Ottawa, York University, Université de Moncton, Université de Saint-Boniface, Collège La Cité and Université Sainte-Anne. One of the major attractions is the opportunity for eligible graduates to apply for Canadian permanent residence. However, completing a programme does not automatically guarantee permanent residency, as applicants must meet additional immigration conditions. The permanent residence application pathway is scheduled to open in winter 2027. Nigeria is not among the 28 African countries eligible for the initiative. However, Nigerians can still apply for Canadian study permits through the regular international student route, subject to the country’s admission and immigration requirements. Udoka, who currently serves as head coach of the Houston Rockets, has established himself as one of the prominent coaching figures in American basketball, with a career shaped by years of playing, coaching and leadership experience. Born on August 9, 1977, in Portland, Oregon, United States, Udoka has Nigerian roots and represented Nigeria in international basketball competitions before transitioning into coaching. His playing career included spells in the NBA, the NBA Development League and professional basketball leagues in Europe. He also played for Nigeria at the 2005 and 2011 FIBA AfroBasket tournaments, helping raise the country’s profile in international basketball. After retiring from professional basketball, Udoka moved into coaching, beginning his NBA coaching career as an assistant with the San Antonio Spurs in 2012. He worked under legendary coach Gregg Popovich, gaining experience in player development, team management and tactical preparation. During his time with San Antonio, the Spurs reached the NBA Finals in 2013 and won the championship in 2014, providing Udoka with valuable experience at the highest level of the sport. He subsequently served as an assistant coach with the Philadelphia 76ers and Brooklyn Nets before joining the Boston Celtics in 2021. Led Boston Celtics to NBA Finals Udoka’s breakthrough as a head coach came in 2021 when he was appointed to lead the Boston Celtics. In his first season, he guided the team to the 2022 NBA Finals, where they faced the Golden State Warriors. Although Boston lost the series 4-2, Udoka earned recognition for transforming the team’s defensive performance and guiding its players through a successful playoff campaign. His achievement made him one of the few coaches to reach the NBA Finals in his first season as a head coach. However, his tenure in Boston ended in September 2022 when the franchise suspended him for the 2022–23 season over violations of team policies. New chapter with Houston Rockets In April 2023, the Houston Rockets appointed Udoka as their head coach, giving him another opportunity to lead an NBA franchise. His appointment marked another significant milestone in his coaching career, as he became responsible for developing a young Houston squad and guiding the franchise towards sustained success. Udoka’s coaching approach has been associated with defensive intensity, accountability and high expectations for players. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Russia’s VTB Opens Bitcoin Trading as Central Bank Finalizes Crypto Test Russian bank VTB began letting brokerage clients buy and sell bitcoin in its investing app on Friday, a day after the Bank of Russia approved the knowledge test every Russian crypto buyer now has to pass. Starting Nov. 27, clients of VTB’s brokerage can trade cryptocurrencies in the VTB My Investments app, the broker said . For now, the trades happen over the counter rather than on an exchange, and access is limited to qualified investors, the legal term for Russians who meet wealth or experience thresholds, who also pass the new test. “In our model, access to cryptocurrencies will require qualified investor status and passing special testing,” Andrei Yatskov, head of brokerage services at VTB, said . He said the test would appear in the app on Nov. 27 and work like the bank’s existing tests for other instruments. VTB handles the buying, storage and record-keeping itself on Russian infrastructure. To trade, clients need to open a separate digital account at VTB’s digital depository, where the crypto is held, on top of their regular brokerage account. The bank received its digital depository and crypto exchange licenses on Oct. 6. “At the start, we will focus on buying and selling cryptocurrencies, and then we will introduce additional services as regulation develops,” Yatskov said. Eight questions before the first trade The launch came quickly after the regulator moved. On Nov. 26, the Bank of Russia approved the first basic standards for brokers and crypto exchange offices, setting the rules for the test. Every investor has to take it, qualified or not, and it is free. Buyers must answer at least seven of eight questions correctly. The standard lays out eight topic blocks, from regulation, technical basics and information security to stablecoins, low-liquidity coins, address labeling and blocked transactions, and volatility, with one question drawn at random from each. Investors who fail can try once more the same day, with different questions. Brokers are barred from sharing the correct answers with clients or telling them which questions they missed. A passing result stays valid for one year from the test date or the latest trade, whichever comes later. The test was the missing piece for Russian banks. When retail buying became legal on Nov. 17 , T-Bank said it was waiting on a market standard for testing, and VTB said it was waiting on the remaining rules. Under the broker standard, the industry’s self-regulatory organization has three working days after publication to send brokers the answer options and correct answers. Ordinary investors still face tight limits once they pass. Non-qualified buyers can only purchase bitcoin, ether and Tether’s USDT, and no more than 300,000 rubles a year through a single intermediary. SPB Exchange sets Dec. 1 start Exchange trading is next. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine New York Wins $1.37 Billion Judgment Against NovaTech Crypto Ponzi Founders A New York judge has ordered the founders of NovaTech, a cryptocurrency investment scheme that targeted Haitian communities, to pay more than $1.37 billion, closing out the state’s case against a couple who fled the country rather than answer it. Justice Anar Rathod Patel of the New York County Supreme Court signed the order on Nov. 24. It holds Cynthia and Eddy Petion and their companies NovaTech Ltd, NovaTech Advisors and NovaPay jointly liable for $1,367,023,585 in disgorgement and interest. New York Attorney General Letitia James announced the win on Wednesday. “Today’s historic judgment finally delivers some semblance of justice for the thousands of New Yorkers who were targeted by this merciless scam,” James said. “NovaTech cruelly targeted immigrant families through faith and community groups with the promise of a better life while robbing them of their life savings.” Where the $1.37 billion figure comes from The award matches what the attorney general’s office asked for in October . The figure starts with the cryptocurrency investors sent to NovaTech’s wallet at payment processor CoinPayments, which totaled about $1.16 billion from August 2019 through May 2023, according to an affirmation filed by the state. Prosecutors subtracted the roughly $26 million NovaTech actually moved to its trading platform, leaving $1.13 billion in principal. Nine percent annual interest from June 2023 through September 2025 added another $232.5 million. NovaTech’s traders lost about $18.2 million of the money they did trade, the filing said. Everything else paid out of the wallet, including so-called returns and recruitment bonuses, came from other investors’ deposits. Cynthia Petion was the only authorized user on the CoinPayments account, and the state says she approved at least $134.5 million in crypto withdrawals to wallets belonging to her and her husband. The judge also ordered the Petions’ earlier venture, AWS Mining, to pay about $1.46 million. Cynthia Petion owes a separate $4.69 million tied to her promotion of that scheme. A NovaTech scheme built on prayer groups AWS Mining sold crypto mining contracts and promised 15% to 20% monthly returns before it collapsed in 2019, according to the attorney general’s office. Promoters recruited through prayer groups, WhatsApp chats and ads in Haitian Creole. NovaTech collapsed in May 2023, and tens of thousands of investors couldn’t withdraw their crypto. The state sued in June 2024. The Petions never answered the complaint. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Trades Near $61,300 as Tech Stock Futures Rally The bitcoin price traded near $61,300 on Friday morning, as tech stock futures jumped ahead of a holiday-shortened session on Wall Street. Bitcoin price is on track for its first weekly gain after seven straight weekly losses, though it is still down about 20% in November. The bitcoin price was up about 1.7% early Friday and set to add 4.8% for the week, Investing.com reported , extending a recovery from a two-year low of $57,325.70 hit earlier in the week. Bitcoin slumped below $57,500 on Wednesday as the Nasdaq sank at the open, before a late rebound in tech shares lifted risk assets. Short sellers helped fuel the bounce. Shorts made up 77% of $84.7 million in bitcoin liquidations over the past day, while futures open interest was little changed. That suggests forced short covering, rather than fresh leverage, supplied much of the lift. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Galaxy Withdraws Call That Bitcoin’s Bear Market Ended in June Galaxy has withdrawn its October call that bitcoin’s bear market ended in June, saying the technical signal behind it failed after seven straight weeks of losses and that the bear market is “very likely not over.” Alex Thorn, Galaxy’s head of firmwide research, laid out the reversal in a report published Wednesday and sent to clients a day earlier. “We withdraw our call that the bear market ended in June,” the report said. “The signal it rested on has failed.” The firm’s Oct. 26 note had argued that bitcoin had entered an accumulation phase. Galaxy said at the time that a weekly close back below the 50-week moving average that was not regained within a month would invalidate its technical case. That is what happened. Bitcoin closed the week ended Nov. 8 at $74,968, 0.7% below the 50-week average, after seven weekly closes above it. It then closed the week ended Nov. 15 below the 200-week average, which Galaxy has described as the floor of past bear markets. Galaxy points to $58,525 The week ended Nov. 22 closed at $61,104, 17.9% below the 50-week average and 10.4% below the 200-week average of $68,159. Bitcoin traded below its July 1 intraday low on Nov. 20 and reached $55,100 on Nov. 21, but the June 30 closing low of $58,525 held on a daily basis through Nov. 22. Galaxy now treats that level as the line to watch. A daily close below $58,525 would be “the start of a move to a materially lower low,” the report said, and the firm would not treat such a close as a buying signal by itself. History is not kind to breaks like that. In the seven prior bear market cases where bitcoin closed below a low that had stood for at least 60 days, the eventual low was at least 17% lower, with a median of 52%. Applied to the June low, that works out to about $48,500 and $28,200. Bitcoin briefly slumped below $57,500 on Wednesday morning as the Nasdaq sank, but it ended the day back above $60,000 and has not posted a daily close below $58,525. It traded near $60,800 on Thursday morning. Late by the clock, early by the depth Galaxy said two readings of the market disagree. By the calendar, this bear is old: Nov. 22 was day 412 since the Oct. 6, 2025, record, longer than the 163 to 406 days from high to low in the four prior bear markets. By depth, it looks unfinished. Bitcoin’s 53% decline compares with drops of 77% to 93% in earlier bears. entertainment.description: Young man with a hard hat holding a red for sale sign outside a building by Pavel Danilyuk for Pexels . My parents’ generation mostly bought land the way their parents did. Someone in the family knew someone in the village. An uncle walked the boundaries. The community remembered who owned what, and if anything went wrong, you had a face to go back to. However, my generation buys land on Instagram. I do not say that to mock anyone. I sell land for a living. When I started in real estate sales in 2023, two years after finishing a Mathematics degree at the University of Ibadan, I assumed buyers would care most about price and location. They do care. But what I hear most often is fear, dressed up as questions. Can I trust you? Is this land real? What happens if I miss a payment? After I pay, will someone come and ask me for more money? A prospective buyer once asked me, before anything else, whether community or family payments would follow after she paid for her plot. She was not asking about the land. She was asking whether the price I quoted was the real price. She had good reason to ask. Lagos State’s Property Protection Law of 2016 made it an offence to demand levies for construction on someone else’s property. Yet the same law still allows a land-owning family, with the family head’s authority, to collect a customary fee for possession, the payment many people know as a “foundation levy”. So the honest answer to her question is not a simple yes or no. It depends on the land, the family, and what has been written down. Most first-time buyers have never been told any of this. That is the gap I keep coming back to. Nobody taught us how to buy land. We learned how to save. Some of us learned how to invest in stocks, crypto or a side business. Powered by CreditRegistry and supported by Afreximbank , the Expo was held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. Themed “Reimagining Africa’s Credit Economy: Unlocking Capital, Trust and Opportunity,” the event provided a platform for conversations on the systems, innovations and partnerships shaping the future of credit across the continent. Building Trust and Expanding Access to Capital Discussions at the Expo explored the role of credible credit information in building trust between lenders and borrowers. Reliable data enables financial institutions to assess risk more effectively and make informed lending decisions, while individuals and businesses with established credit histories are better positioned to demonstrate their credit worthiness. The conversations also considered the financing constraints facing micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). Despite their contribution to employment and economic activity, many small businesses continue to encounter barriers to affordable financing. Improving access to relevant financial products and strengthening credit information systems remain important to addressing these gaps. Technology, Financial Inclusion and the Next Generation Digital innovation and data intelligence featured prominently in discussions about the future of credit. Alternative credit assessment approaches have the potential to broaden access for individuals and businesses with limited formal credit histories. entertainment.title: As Nigeria Rethinks Teacher Education, Tunji Olowolafe Makes a Case for Better-Prepared Educators
entertainment.description: What makes a good teacher? Beyond knowing a subject, a good teacher can understand students, inspire confidence, and help young people discover what they are capable of becoming. It was this broader responsibility of educators that Dr. Tunji Olowolafe explored while delivering the 2026 Convocation Lecture at the Sikiru Adetona College of Education, Science and Technology (SACOETEC), Omu-Ajose, Ogun State. Speaking on Monday, 23 November 2026, on the theme “The Dual-Mandate NCE-Degree Programme: Prospects, Challenges and the Future of Teacher Education in Nigeria,” he described the programme as an important opportunity to reposition teacher education. For decades, Colleges of Education depended on university affiliations to award Bachelor’s degrees, despite many possessing the academic capacity to run such programmes. The Federal Colleges of Education Act 2023 changed this, empowering eligible institutions to award degrees independently. Under the Dual-Mandate programme, students can complete three years of NCE training and proceed to another two years for a Bachelor’s degree in Education. Dr. Olowolafe explained that combining practical teaching skills with deeper academic knowledge would produce better-prepared educators. However, he cautioned that institutional autonomy must be supported by sustained funding, improved curricula and professional development. With Nigeria facing an estimated shortage of one million teachers, he also called for greater integration of vocational education, artificial intelligence and digital skills into learning. “AI can explain a quadratic equation at midnight, but it cannot offer the steady, empathetic guidance of a caring adult,” he said, emphasizing that artificial intelligence must complement, not replace, the human qualities of effective teaching. During the lecture, Dr. Olowolafe announced that the Tunji Olowolafe Foundation would establish a fully equipped, solar-powered Gbemisola Olowolafe Memorial ICT Centre (GOMTECH) with high-speed internet connectivity at SACOETEC. The Foundation is also committed to recognising academic excellence and outstanding teaching at the College. This includes recognising the College’s first-class degree graduates and NCE distinction holders, alongside the overall best NCE and degree graduates. Lecturers, selected based on student ratings, will also be honoured for their teaching contributions. The initiative builds on the Foundation’s existing investment in education, including Project Digi-Teach at Ekiti State University and GOMTECH in Are-Ekiti. For Dr. Olowolafe, the commitment to educators is also deeply personal. His mother was a teacher, his elder sister taught for years at Baptist Academy, Lagos, and his late wife, Gbemisola Olowolafe, was a lifelong educator. He recalled the influence of teachers who shaped his own experience, particularly Mr. Soewu of Methodist Boys’ High School , whose patience helped students understand difficult concepts without humiliation. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). A B or a C in his Cambridge A-levels felt like a possibility he wasn’t ready to entertain, so he didn’t write the exams. A few years later, at 23, he has graduated from the University of Ibadan with a B.Sc. in Statistics, First-Class Honours and a CGPA of 3.65/4.0. Somewhere along the way, he decided that fear was no longer going to make his decisions for him. When Williams got into UI, he had a rather ambitious plan: become the Best Graduating Student in his faculty. Getting there would require more than good intentions. There were 5:30am wake-ups, difficult Statistics courses, friends who became unofficial tutors, a ChatGPT Pro subscription in 300 level, job offers he turned down and one Demography exam that kept him awake for 36 hours. University, as it turns out, came with quite a few plot twists. In this interview with BellaNaija, Williams takes us through the habits, people and decisions that shaped his academic journey. He also tells us whether he got that coveted top spot, what he learnt from the opportunities he put on hold, and what he would tell another student hoping to graduate with First-Class Honours. If that’s a goal you’re working towards, you may want to take notes. Literally or otherwise. Williams Alamu celebrates graduating with First-Class Honours in Statistics from the University of Ibadan. At what point did you realise you were chasing a record-breaking grade? Was it a goal from Day 1, or did it evolve? It was a goal from day one, actually. When I gained admission into the University of Ibadan, I already had my mind set on graduating as the Best Graduating Student in my faculty. I knew becoming the overall Best Graduating Student in the university would require an extraordinary amount of work, but I felt being the best in my faculty was something I wanted to work towards. And, of course, that would also mean graduating as the best student in my department. The motivation behind that goal goes back to shortly after secondary school, when my parents enrolled me in a Cambridge A-level programme. I went into it hoping to achieve three A-stars, but Chemistry was a major struggle. As the examinations approached, I became increasingly worried about my performance. I think I was more afraid of not meeting my own expectations than I was of the examination itself. The thought of getting a B or C frightened me so much that I eventually decided not to sit for the examinations. Interim coach Rick Stockstill has addressed the possibility of making a quarterback change if Florida State’s offense continues to struggle. Florida State Quarterback Situation Draws Attention Ashton Daniels remains Florida State’s starting quarterback entering Friday’s matchup. This one-year deal could reach $6.5 million, marking the largest contract for a position player in president of baseball operations Peter Bendix tenure. Since the regular season concluded, this marks the initial known free agent signing executed by the franchise. Although this transaction addresses a particular weakness, the front office must go further to build upon an 80-win campaign. Fixing the Left-Handed Gap Sanchez offers a right-handed bat that Miami desperately needs against southpaws. His batting average sat at .209 for the World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers, yet he achieved a far superior .801 OPS against left-handed pitching. This specific skill set targets a key vulnerability in the lineup. Sanchez turns 34 next week and will likely serve as a backup to starting catcher Joe Mack. His role may shift to designated hitter or late-game pinch-hitter duties to maximize his offensive value while limiting his defensive exposure. Sandy Alcantara stays the ace, while Eury Perez demonstrated moments of brilliance despite a volatile season. Following a neck injury that ended his season early, Max Meyer is anticipated to be prepared for spring training. Beyond those three, the depth is thin. sports.description: COLUMBUS, OH - SEPTEMBER 24: Pittsburgh Penguins forward Atley Calvert (84) controls the puck as Columbus Blue Jackets forward Adam Fantilli (19) gives chase during a preseason NHL game between the Columbus Blue Jackets and Pittsburgh Penguins on September 24, 2025, at Nationwide Arena in Columbus, OH. (Photo by Nick Wosika/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Penguins announced a recall from the minors this morning, forward Atley Calvert joins the NHL roster for the first time. Forward Atley Calvert has been recalled from the @WBSPenguins (AHL). pic.twitter.com/TYYH4DzjaD — Pittsburgh Penguins (@penguins) November 27, 2026 It’s a great story for the 23-year old slowly but surely climbing the ranks. The undrafted Calvert started out with an AHL contract with the Pens back in 2024. He split time between the ECHL and AHL in his first pro season. Last year, he became a key player in Wilkes-Barre, scoring 38 points in 70 games and excelling in a variety of roles, including playing some center when the team was short and needed the help. Calvert was rewarded with his first NHL contract last off-season. He’s been one of the top players to Wilkes-Barre this year, producing 15 points in 20 games. “He has, really, a lot of pro qualities to his game that I think can translate,” assistant GM Jason Spezza said back at training camp . “He’s a winger that can play center. He’s a bit of a Swiss Army knife for us. So, a guy the coaches really lean on down there in different ways. I think at times maybe it’s the short end of the stick offensively because he’s so reliable defensively, and in kind of the roles that coaches like to use guys.” Many players have been recalled, which hasn’t always meant finding time in the game lineup. That doesn’t look to be the case this time around, despite having Justin Brazeau and Andrei Kuzmenko on hand, the Pens put Calvert in a position that suggests he will make his NHL debut tonight in Buffalo. All of that pales compared to another tangible step of the youth movement encroaching on the Penguins. Pittsburgh only has a roster spot available as long as Egor Chinakhov remains on IR, so Calvert’s first taste of NHL action could be short-lived. However, it likely won’t be his only opportunity to play NHL games this season since it’s expected the Pens will be shifting gears in the near future and starting to trade away veterans on the roster and open up more places for younger players like Calvert. Another step in that journey looks like it will take place tonight.

sports.title: Raiders defense is doing well in this area
sports.description: (Photo by Edward Monigan IV/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders’ defense, overall, has been having a rough season. However, the unit is doing one thing very well — creating turnovers. Las Vegas has 17 takeaways, which is tied for the third most in the NFL. Many of the Raiders’ takeaways are coming when it counts. According to this X Post, Las Vegas has 10 takeaways in the fourth quarter of games. That leads the league by three. NFL defenses ranked by 4th quarter takeaways: pic.twitter.com/WPp6dQq4Hd — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) November 24, 2026 Las Vegas has compiled those 10 fourth-quarter takeaways in six of their 11 games. They got fourth-quarter takeaways in all four of their wins this season and two came in defeats. Of course, they had four against the New Orleans Saints in a Week 3 win. So, this is a heck of a formula for the Raiders to find a way to win. If they can get their opponents to cough up the ball late, Las Vegas has a real chance to win. Let’s see if they can force the Cleveland Browns into a late turnover on Sunday night.

sports.title: Real Madrid set to block exit of four players in January; two allowed to leave – report
sports.description: Real Madrid set to block exit of four players in January; two allowed to leave – report With the January transfer window just around the corner, Real Madrid are bracing themselves for relative peace and quiet, especially after a busy summer. The club are not expected to sign any new players in the winter transfer window. However, it is worth mentioning that a series of existing stars are facing an uncertain future and could leave in January. Endrick, Thiago Pitarch and Brahim Diaz are some of the many Real Madrid players facing an uncertain future at Santiago Bernabeu. Real Madrid, though, have a plan. Four exits to be blocked According to Miguel Serrano (h/t Defensa Central ), Real Madrid have made their mind up, as far as the club’s dealings in the January transfer window is concerned. The club are expected to block the exit of all the players who have been linked with a move away from Bernabeu this season, including Endrick. Brahim Diaz won’t be allowed to leave Real Madrid in January. (Photo by Fran Santiago/Getty Images) The exits of Trent Alexander-Arnold, Pitarch and Diaz are also expected to be blocked, as Jose Mourinho consider all of them key parts of the setup. It appears Mourinho is wary that any injury crisis during the second half of the campaign could make these players handy, as they offer plenty of quality to the table. Endrick, in particular, boasts immense talent and has been linked with a move away. But he has the backing of Mourinho . The same goes for Pitarch, even though the midfielder has barely played any football this season. Two exceptions to Real Madrid Serrano adds that Real Madrid have made an exception to this policy for two players in the form of Ferland Mendy and Raul Asencio. Both these defenders are allowed to leave the club in the January transfer window, having failed to find themselves in Mourinho’s plans this season. Ferland Mendy is no longer needed at Real Madrid. (Photo by Jose Manuel Alvarez Rey/Getty Images) Asencio, for one, has struggled with injuries and several off-field controversies. He has also looked like a shadow of his former self. His departure, therefore, could be a major positive for Real Madrid. Mendy, on the other hand, has a lucrative salary at Bernabeu despite having his entire career at Real Madrid marred by injuries . With Marc Cucurella and Alvaro Carreras, Real Madrid look quite stacked at left-back and no longer require the services of Mendy, whose contract expires in 2028. These are, however, still early days and if a lucrative market opportunity comes, Real Madrid will not shy away from making a few more exceptions.

sports.title: FC Cincinnati looks to clinch series against Nashville SC
sports.description: FC Cincinnati stunned Major League Soccer experts with its 1-0 win over Nashville SC in the first game of their best-of-three playoff series at Nashville’s GEODIS park. They will now have two chances to move on to the Eastern Conference semifinals. The first is at home, 6:30 p.m. Nov. 28 at TQL Stadium. Game 3, if needed, will be 8 p.m. Dec. 2 back in Nashville. As the No. 9 seed in the Eastern Conference, this will be the last home game for Cincinnati in the conference playoffs. The only team in the Western Conference they could host in the MLS Cup final is Real Salt Lake, the No. 9 seed. The team is ready for what could be their last home game. “Trying to make sure that we step on the field with a really strong mindset,” said head coach Pat Noonan. “I know there's confidence, but there's also still a respect factor for how strong Nashville is, and we need to find ways to have our fan base lively, and a lot of times that comes with our play. It’s always nice to be having home games in the playoffs, and having that energy, that feel around the city, so hopefully we can take advantage of it.” Sure, Cincinnati’s winning goal came on a lucky break via a disastrous mistake by Nashville in the seventh minute of play, when Patrick Yazbek made a panicked back pass into his own net from 18 yards. But Cincinnati served notice with its defense the rest of the way, shutting out the best regular-season team in MLS history. Nashville had 22 shots, six on goal. Roman Celentano made six saves and the defense did the rest. Tom Bogert of the Athletic wrote this week, “How repeatable is all of this? I don’t know. sports.description: Sirianni celebrates Nick Sirianni gave Cowboys fans some salt for their Thanksgiving meals. The Eagles coach, moments after defeating their rivals on a 59-yard field goal with two seconds left for a 39-38 victory , beelined for the field-level suites at AT&T Stadium in Dallas in a quick reminder of what just happened. Sirianni’s celebration was filled with some one-finger salutes from the Cowboys faithful and a short-lived one, as he was whisked away by Philadelphia’s chief security officer “Big Dom” DiSandro before things got too hairy. Nick Sirianni celebrated in front of the Cowboys fans after the Eagles comeback win ( FOX) pic.twitter.com/mR8isTM2Zh — SportsCenter (@SportsCenter) November 27, 2026 Not that DiSandro didn’t get his licks in. The Herculean 34-year-old was caught trolling former Eagles defensive backs coach and current Cowboys defense coordinator Christian Parker, who recently had his play calling duties taken away by Dallas, before the game, teasing him with an Eagles hat. The win completed the largest-ever Thanksgiving Day comeback in NFL history, with the Eagles trailing 31-10 in the third quarter. Quarterback Joe Milton, in just his third start for Philadelphia — and against his old team — threw for 331 yards and three touchdowns, while adding a rushing score. “He played his butt off,” Sirianni said. “He played really good, made some throws that only he can make. sports.description: Alexander Isak has scored 10 goals for Liverpool this season (NICOLAS TUCAT) Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola has praised Alexander Isak's response to his exacting tactical demands after the forward reached 10 goals for the club this season. The 27-year-old had a turbulent, injury-hit first campaign at Anfield but is now showing why Liverpool paid £125 million ($164 million) to prise him from Newcastle last year. In September, Iraola spoke about how his "fights" with the Sweden international were about the work he needed to do off the ball. Over the subsequent two months there has been a marked change in Isak's ability to fulfil Iraola's demands. In Wednesday's 3-0 Champions League win against Club Brugge, Isak's pressing before his opener unsettled goalkeeper Yann Sommer. He also scored a second goal late in the game. "He has definitely improved a lot on the ball and without the ball," Iraola told reporters ahead of Sunday's Merseyside derby at Everton. "He is understanding better the press and the better he understands the press the less he has to run also. "Also on the ball we are using him much better in possession, he is linking up play very well. Technically he is a very nice player so I think we have to use him not just in the finishing side, he can be very important in our build-up." Iraola, in his first season at Anfield, praised Isak's performance during last week's 4-0 humbling of Manchester United, which lifted Liverpool to fourth in the table, as well as his display in Belgium. "I think he is understanding everything and is ready to learn and even improve more and it is a good sign," the Spaniard said on Friday. Former Bournemouth manager Iraola is looking forward to his first taste of a Merseyside derby. "I know I haven't lived this derby, but it doesn't take a lot when you are here to perceive that it's a big game for everyone involved," he said. "I'm very happy to be part of it and I hope I enjoy it, and to enjoy it there is only one way –- that is to win the game." sports.title: Club pro makes hole-in-one at Australian PGA, wins $160K BMW
sports.description: The hole-in-one looked like a mistake the moment the ball left Robbie Minns’ club. The payoff? A brand-new BMW, worth about $160,000. Minns, a club professional at Camden Golf Club in southwest Sydney, stepped to the par-3 18th Friday during the second round of the BMW Australian PGA Championship at The Lakes Golf Club and immediately took one hand off the club after impact. Turns out there was nothing wrong with the shot. The ball landed in the middle of the green, tracked toward the flag and disappeared into the cup, setting off a wild celebration from the group of friends following Minns around the course. The ace came with quite a bonus. Minns won a new BMW X5 valued at roughly $160,000 for making the hole-in-one. He became the second player in as many years to claim the tournament’s BMW hole-in-one prize after Daniel Gale made an ace at Royal Queensland last year. More: It's time for golf's silly season. sports.title: Tottenham dealt major blow as Roberto De Zerbi rules winger Savio out of the Christmas schedule with hamstring injury
sports.description: Tottenham Hotspur v Crystal Palace FC - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Roberto De Zerbi has confirmed that Savio will miss Tottenham's festive fixtures and could be sidelined for up to 80 days with a hamstring injury. The Brazilian winger broke down less than half an hour after returning from the same problem in the 2-0 win over Ipswich, leaving Spurs without one of their most expensive summer signings during the busiest stretch of the season. De Zerbi delivers grim Savio update Savio came off the bench in the 64th minute of last Saturday's victory over Ipswich, but was forced off with two minutes left after a recurrence of the injury that had ruled him out of four league games. Asked at his press conference ahead of Sunday's trip to Sunderland whether the winger could miss the rest of the year, De Zerbi said: "Yeah, I think so. Unfortunately it's a tough situation to accept. He's a new guy and he's suffering with these new injuries. But this is football, if you see other European clubs they're all suffering these injuries." 'He will be crucial for us' The Ipswich win was Savio's first appearance in six weeks, according to BBC Sport , and there had already been fears that he faced weeks on the sidelines after he left the pitch visibly distraught. De Zerbi has now admitted he cannot put a date on his return. "Now he needs time. He needs hard work with the medical staff," the Italian added. "Then in 50 days, 60 days, 80 days, I don't know, when he comes back, he will be crucial for us in the last step of the season." Frustrating start to Spurs career The 22-year-old has endured a frustrating start to life in north London since his summer move from Manchester City in a deal that could reach £85 million. He has featured in only five of Tottenham's 11 Premier League games and is still waiting for his first league goal or assist. Savio did score and assist on his debut in a 5-1 Carabao Cup win over Charlton in August. His absence adds to an injury list that already includes Mathys Tel, Mykhailo Mudryk, Xavi Simons and Wilson Odobert, while Lucas Bergvall is a doubt with illness. Spurs face busy December Tottenham, who are 10th after four wins from their past five matches, visit 18th-placed Sunderland at the Stadium of Light. They then host Fulham on December 3 before welcoming champions Arsenal for the north London derby three days later.

technology.title: Smartphone shipments face another bleak year before modest 2028 comeback
technology.description: Global smartphone shipments are forecast to fall 14 percent this year and another 6 percent in 2027, with a recovery not expected until 2028. That's the outlook from Counterpoint Research's latest Smartphone Market Outlook Tracker , which points to rising memory costs and constrained supplies as continuing pressure on handset makers and buyers. The downturn was particularly sharp in the third quarter: IDC and Omdia estimated year-on-year shipment declines of 22 percent and 20 percent respectively, as rising prices and component shortages squeezed the market. Don't expect things to get better in the short term, as Counterpoint forecasts another 6 percent drop during 2027. But it believes that the market may see a 6 percent rebound in 2028, as memory supplies improve, pricing begins to stabilize, and pent-up demand for replacement phones returns. The 2026 outlook has been shaped by sharply rising component costs, particularly for DRAM and NAND flash. According to IDC , memory costs have risen approximately 350 percent since last year and are still climbing. As Reg readers will be well aware by now, this has been blamed on the memory manufacturers prioritizing output of high-margin chips to go into AI servers and GPU accelerators, creating a shortage of the mainstream components that are needed for devices like PCs and phones. Vendors have responded by raising prices, reducing memory configurations, and withdrawing lower-cost models. As The Register previously reported , memory costs accounted for almost 60 percent of the total bill of materials in sub-$400 smartphones during Q1 of 2026. For 2027, Counterpoint warns the outlook is for continued tight mobile DRAM supply, further price increases for low-power DDR (LPDDR) memory, and limited evidence to suggest short-term capacity increases. "The 2026 decline was initially expected to mark the low point of the cycle, but the memory situation has remained more restrictive than anticipated," said principal analyst Yang Wang. "Mobile memory allocation is still being displaced by AI and server demand, while higher costs are taking longer to move through handset portfolios and retail channels. The result is a much weaker 2027, particularly for lower priced devices and price sensitive markets." Global shipments are forecast to rebound by 6 percent in 2028, but that would bring shipments only roughly back to this year's already shrunken level, rather than hitting the peak of previous years. Counterpoint cautions that the scale of the rebound will depend on how quickly lower component costs translate into retail pricing. A speedy improvement in mobile memory allocation during the second half of 2027 could bring replacement demand forward and swell shipments, but continued competition from the AI market or another round of handset price increases would hinder recovery. technology.title: Bill for Birmingham's Oracle debacle reaches £128M
technology.description: Birmingham City Council faces a £128.1 million bill for its disastrous transition from SAP to Oracle – more than six times the original estimate for a project that contributed to its financial collapse. Papers presented to its Audit Committee this week put the combined cost of the original implementation, which went live in 2022, and this year's reimplementation at £128.1 million, against £19.96 million forecast in the 2019 business case [PDF]. The report , from program director Philip Macpherson, said the project's funding allocation had previously reached £157 million. The report said the new Oracle Fusion system went live in August without any priority-one or "showstopper" issues. "The program has now moved into the Post Go Live Support phase where [it] continues to provide extra support but slowly transitions towards 'Business As Usual' operating procedures," the report said. It is an understatement to say the same was not true of the first attempt to move the council's finance, HR, and payroll systems off its legacy R/3 SAP system to more modern software. The first project started in 2019 and was supposed to go live in April 2021, but was delayed by a year. After the council started to use the system in April 2022, it soon became beset by a series of serious problems. Although the council had planned to implement Oracle "out-of-the-box," it created several customizations, including a bank reconciliation system that failed to function properly. The council struggled to understand its cash position and was unable to produce auditable accounts . It has spent more than £5 million on manual workaround labor . The system move also contributed to it becoming effectively bankrupt , an event it failed to foresee due to the malfunctioning finance system. It later emerged that officials ignored a "red" warning prior to the go-live date. They were explicitly told the system could cause late payments, a failure to collect debt, and incorrect accounting if it went live. Officials gave the go-ahead regardless. The council decided to reimplement Oracle from scratch, while running the current system as best it could and implementing off-the-shelf software CivicaPay , now rebranded as Civica Income Management. Despite the apparently trouble-free relaunch, the true cost to the council is likely higher than the projected £128.1 million implementation bill. For a start, the original £19 million budget was supposed to support the software implementation for schools , but that was excluded from the reimplementation. Secondly, the council expected significant savings from moving to Oracle in 2022 through greater efficiency. The 2019 business case booked £27 million in savings from 2019 to 2031, for example. A 2024 analysis by Audit Reform Lab, based at the University of Sheffield, estimated that the disaster's direct and indirect financial impact, including lost savings and deteriorating tax collection, would reach £216.5 million by April 2026. technology.title: UK government rejects national consultation on AI datacenters
technology.description: The UK government has rejected calls for a UK-wide public consultation on the environmental impacts of AI datacenters, despite a petition attracting more than 39,000 signatures. Campaign group Protect the Wild launched the petition last month, calling for a national consultation that would consider whether further expansion should be restricted, paused, or halted until those impacts are properly understood and addressed. The nonprofit says the petition smashed the 10,000 signature threshold above which a government response is required in just three days, and the total stood at over 39,000 as this article was being prepared. In its response, published on November 23, the government ruled out the requested UK-wide environmental consultation, saying individual projects' impacts should be addressed through the planning process. It pointed instead to a separate consultation on its draft datacenter planning policy, open until January 8, 2027. "Datacenters are vital to the UK's digital economy. They underpin the digital services that people rely on every day, including public services, healthcare and the way people work. technology.title: Europe's AI sovereignty push: Lots of cloud, not much silver lining
technology.description: Europe's IT spending is growing more slowly than the global average, according to Gartner, whose analysts warn that the region's push for tech sovereignty faces commercial and technological obstacles. Gartner forecasts European IT spending of $1.57 trillion in 2027, up 9.9 percent from 2026, compared with worldwide growth of 15 percent to $7.35 trillion. For 2026, it estimates spending growth of 20.7 percent in North America and 13.7 percent in China. "The world seems to be racing towards this AI goal of where the large language model provider is going to be, and the race seems to be between North American-based providers and some Asia Pacific providers," John-David Lovelock, Distinguished VP Analyst at Gartner, told The Register . He said Europe had traditionally trailed in IT uptake. "We saw that happen when global sourcing, cloud, and software as a service all came along. It's down to the pushback against the idea of creative destruction," where new technologies replace old ones. Europe's fastest growing categories are datacenter systems, forecast to grow 29.7 percent in 2027, and infrastructure as a service, at 26.7 percent. Even so, Lovelock does not expect Europe to compete with North America and China on AI investment. "For AI provision, Europe is going to be behind, and there won't be a way to catch up," he said. "The AI datacenters, the large language models, the foundational models, the tools and techniques for building out AI are all being centered outside of Europe, but enterprises don't need to do that. So the question becomes: regardless of where the source of the AI is coming from, can the enterprises actually adopt and use it? In one sense, Europe will be behind in the provision of AI, but it need not be behind in the use." The gap nonetheless complicates Europe's push to reduce its dependence on US technology suppliers. The European Union has introduced new rules to encourage tech buyers to favor sovereign tech over the dominant tech vendors, but Lovelock doubts they will move spending much. "Sovereignty is a wonderful flag that we fly on the front of a building. IT is running in the basement. CIOs are not going to buy a second-best solution that costs more simply because it's sovereign. "They are not going to break any laws, but they are not going to make a decision that puts their company in a worse position at a higher cost. While sovereignty gets [vendors] on the list, it doesn't assure that they get purchased," he told us. Earlier this month, Gartner predicted that by 2029, more than 90 percent of EU organizations will have a digital sovereignty strategy, but argued that a fully sovereign technology stack remains out of reach. "The global technology supply chain is too interconnected, and many critical dependencies cannot be replaced at a commercially viable scale," said Bettina Tratz-Ryan, VP analyst at Gartner. ®

technology.title: AI boom leaves network operators waiting up to 18 months for kit
technology.description: The AI building boom is driving up optical networking equipment prices and stretching delivery times to as much as 18 months, according to network operator RETN. RETN says that network operators and telcos are now directly competing with AI datacenters for chips and other components. As Reg readers will be aware, memory prices have soared by four or five times over the past year or so, but RETN says optical networking equipment prices have risen by around 50 percent since the start of 2026. Worse are the extended delivery times, with optical network kit that used to arrive within three months now taking 12 to 15, and some orders taking up to 18 months. This is as bad as, if not worse than, the shortages during the pandemic, when chip supply problems left network vendors unable to fulfill orders . The issue now is that because of the AI boom, demand is outpacing supplies. In its report, "AI, Connected," RETN says developers building outside established datacenter hubs may need to involve network carriers two to five years before opening. The sudden demand for network kit from hyperscalers and AI campuses is only one factor, RETN says. Raw material shortages, skilled labor shortages, energy constraints, geopolitical tensions, and logistical challenges are also compounding the issue. However, it concedes that many carriers didn't help themselves by previously postponing network upgrades to cut expenditure. That work has now become unavoidable at the worst possible time. Network diversity is now seen as a must-have, the report says. Where customers were once satisfied with two routes to long-haul destinations, they expect operators to provide four or more redundant routes now. The aim is to prevent a single failure from taking down critical services. Multiple connections are only useful protection if they avoid shared physical failure points, such as the same ducts or cable routes. A diverse circuit might cost €1,800 ($1,975) a month instead of €600 ($658), it claims, but an outage could prove far more costly. RETN also says AI datacenters are moving away from populated areas to remote locations, where access to suitable land, power and water may be easier to come by. Hyperscalers are building in the Nordics, where land is affordable, the climate is cooler, and plenty of renewable energy is available. Remote sites may lack the fiber infrastructure needed to connect them to other datacenters and customers. The Register reported on this issue earlier this year. For sites close to cities, developers often fund the fiber themselves, which adds just a few percent to the total project cost. But over longer distances, the case becomes harder to make, and carriers are understandably reluctant to build a long-haul route to serve a single remote site. technology.title: Royal Navy orders £142M in minehunting drones from US supplier
technology.description: Britain's Royal Navy is investing £142 million ($185 million) in underwater drones to tackle sea mines, but the contract has gone to an American defense supplier. The Ministry of Defence (MoD) says that the UK's ability to protect vital sea routes will be strengthened through the procurement of these Uncrewed Underwater Vehicles (UUVs). These will form part of the Royal Navy's move toward a " Hybrid Navy " comprising a mix of crewed, uncrewed, and autonomous platforms in order to meet future challenges. The UUV selected for the job is the REMUS 620 , built by Huntington Ingalls Industries (HII), the largest military shipbuilding company in the United States. HII has a facility at Portchester, on the south coast of England, but is still a US-owned company. We asked the MoD how the award fits its pledge to prioritize buying British wherever possible, and what share of the contract's value will support UK industry. The contract includes HII's Sea Launcher automated launch and recovery systems and will bring support services previously delivered overseas to the UK. HII says it will support 15 jobs, while the MoD identifies Portchester among the locations benefiting. HII says this is the largest international order in its 25-year history of supplying uncrewed systems. The MoD has previously acquired REMUS 100, REMUS 300, and REMUS 600 vehicles for mine countermeasure operations. The new vehicles will locate sea mines to support clearance operations and help keep shipping routes open. By using drones to comb a body of water for explosive devices, the Royal Navy's crews can be kept a safe distance from any potential immediate threat. Traditionally, this work has been conducted by specialist crewed ships such as the Hunt class or Sandown class , but these are being retired from service in favor of uncrewed systems. The Royal Navy also operates SWEEP , an uncrewed boat towing equipment that mimics a ship's magnetic, acoustic, and electric signatures to trigger mines from a safe distance. The new REMUS underwater vehicles can be sent ahead of other vessels to search beneath the surface, making minehunting operations safer, faster and more flexible, according to the MoD. "This investment strengthens our ability to protect freedom of navigation, which is critical to our security and our economy," said Defence Secretary Wes Streeting MP. Like others in the portfolio, REMUS 620 resembles a naval torpedo. It is capable of operating at depths of 600 meters and has an endurance of up to 110 hours on a single mission. The drones will be integrated with SeeTrack and Neptune software developed by SeeByte in the UK, which is already used by the Royal Navy. In trials announced in October 2025, a REMUS 620 demonstrated launch and recovery using a submerged test fixture replicating a Virginia-class submarine's torpedo tube. The work could enable submarines to deploy and retrieve underwater drones on future missions. ®
